clue.text: Machine parts shielded by 11

explanation.surface: Components of some machinery are protected by a medieval warrior.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 is the knight-at-arms; heraldic bearings are the devices displayed on a knight's shield.
explanation.definitionFit: Ball or roller races in machines are one sense; armorial devices on a shield, in heraldry, are the other.

clue.text: Those who dispossess successful Orientals

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for East, home of Orientals
the successful are the victors

explanation.surface: Landlords throwing out tenants are winning Easterners.
explanation.definitionFit: Landlords who throw tenants out of their homes by legal process take away their possession.

clue.text: Batty sort of extortion?

parts.note: a tennis bat is a racket, so a 'batty' kind of extortion is a protection scheme run by a gang

explanation.surface: A crazy form of blackmail.
explanation.definitionFit: Organised extortion by a criminal gang, a protection scheme, is the crime meant.

clue.text: Find the way to raise the terrible match attendance ?

indicators.note: in a down clue, to raise a word is to write it bottom to top, so it reads backwards

parts.note: Ivan the Terrible was the sixteenth-century Russian tsar
the gate is the number of spectators at a sports match

explanation.surface: Working out how to boost a dreadful crowd at a football game.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer or plot a course is to work out the route to a destination.

clue.text: Secret agent's (or Tom's) point of view

definitions.text: Secret agent's (or Tom's) point of view

parts.words: Secret agent's (or Tom's) point of view
parts.note: a spy, or a Peeping Tom, watches through a small opening in a door or wall

explanation.surface: How an undercover operative, or a voyeur, sees the world.
explanation.definitionFit: A small peephole in a door lets someone watch unseen, as a snooper would.

clue.text: Decree Dorian's metamorphosis

indicators.note: a metamorphosis is a change of form, so the letters of the name are rearranged

parts.note: the name Dorian, the possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: An order that Dorian Gray should be transformed.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to order or decree officially.

clue.text: Light entertainment?

explanation.surface: Something easy and diverting to watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Light means pale, as of complexion or hair; entertainment means a funfair with rides and stalls.

clue.text: Keeps on asking: Is rep going up the smaller streets ?

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the words are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
streets made smaller, abbreviated, are STS

explanation.surface: A salesman repeatedly asks whether he is heading up the side roads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' turns IS and REP together to give PERSI; 'asking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To persist is to continue steadily despite opposition.

clue.text: Where in London anti-flood precaution came by air?

indicators.note: the ark came into the aircraft, so one is placed inside the other

parts.note: a plane is how one travels by air
Noah built the ark as a precaution against the Flood

explanation.surface: A London location where Noah's ark arrived by aeroplane.
explanation.walkthrough: PARK LANE is a grand street in Mayfair, London, and a square on the British Monopoly board.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous West End street is a location in the capital.

clue.text: CID's maybe got one up its sleeve!

indicators.note: maybe signals that these letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: The detectives have a secret trick ready to use.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is Britain's Criminal Investigation Department; its letters with the S are rearranged. A gramophone record is kept in a paper sleeve.
explanation.definitionFit: A gramophone record is stored inside a cardboard or paper cover.

clue.text: The Forsaken Mere-man (Keats, not Arnold)

parts.note: Matthew Arnold wrote The Forsaken Merman; Keats's forsaken man by the mere is the armed knight of La Belle Dame sans Merci

explanation.surface: A title of Matthew Arnold's poem, credited instead to Keats.
explanation.walkthrough: In Keats's ballad a knight is found alone and palely loitering by a lake (a mere), forsaken by the fairy lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats's poem opens by addressing an armed medieval knight abandoned by the lakeside.

clue.text: Latitude to change outcome of an endless trial with 400 lire

indicators.note: the gathered letters are to change their order
endless means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: CCCC is 400 in Roman numerals, C being 100

explanation.surface: Gamblers try to alter the result of an unfinished court case with Italian money.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIA (trial without its last letter), CCCC and LIRE are mixed together; 'outcome of an' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: The polar circle near 66 degrees north is a parallel, a line of latitude.

clue.text: This band is not allowed in traffic

definitions.text: This band is not allowed in traffic

parts.words: This band is not allowed in traffic
parts.note: put this word before 'band' and the result is smuggled goods, prohibited in trade

explanation.surface: A group of musicians is banned from the roads.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for against, also a rebel in Nicaragua, joins band to make smuggled goods.

clue.text: Designs to block economies in floor-coverings?

indicators.note: the cuts are made in the floor-coverings, so the lino comes first

parts.note: lino, short for linoleum, is a floor covering
economies are cuts in spending

explanation.surface: Plans to stop cost savings on carpets and vinyl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to block' hints that a linocut is printed from a carved block.
explanation.definitionFit: A print made from a design carved into a linoleum block is a linocut.

clue.text: He's rude, perhaps, when shown in…

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters might be ordered otherwise

parts.note: the letters of He's, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A man is ill-mannered, maybe, when guided into a room.
explanation.definitionFit: Shown in means escorted inside, which is what an usher does.

clue.text: Revolt — like Shelley's skylark?

explanation.surface: A rebellion compared with the soaring bird in Shelley's ode.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shelley's To a Skylark the bird flies 'higher still and higher / From the earth'.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolt is a rebellion; Shelley's skylark is forever ascending into the sky.

clue.text: … his writing on science causing dissensions

parts.note: SC is an abbreviation for science
MS, manuscript, is a piece of writing

explanation.surface: A man's essay on science provokes quarrels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places his writing after science; 'causing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Splits within a group, especially a church, come from disagreement and dissent.

clue.text: The sort of shoe-string that bewitched Herrick

definitions.text: The sort of shoe-string that bewitched Herrick

parts.words: The sort of shoe-string that bewitched Herrick
parts.note: in Herrick's poem Delight in Disorder, an untidily tied shoelace bewitches the poet more than neat art

explanation.surface: A question about the kind of shoelace that enchanted the poet Robert Herrick.
explanation.definitionFit: Herrick praised a negligently tied lace showing 'wild civility', a heedless sort of shoe-string.

clue.text: What the 11's 24 certainly was not

parts.note: the knight's lady in Keats is La Belle Dame sans Merci, the beautiful lady without pity

explanation.surface: A remark on the character of a knight's lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Sans merci means without mercy, so the lady was anything but compassionate.

clue.text: Might gardeners name 'it " Five o'clock sprinkler "?

definitions.text: Might gardeners name 'it " Five o'clock sprinkler "?

parts.note: five o'clock is the traditional British teatime
a rose is the perforated spray nozzle on a watering can

explanation.surface: Would a gardener give a flower a name like Teatime Watering Can?
explanation.definitionFit: A rose variety with a scent likened to tea is a garden flower gardeners name.

clue.text: "" Life… Stains the white of Eternity " (Shelley)

definitions.text: "" Life… Stains the white of Eternity " (Shelley)

parts.words: "" Life… Stains the white of Eternity " (Shelley)
parts.note: a quotation from Shelley's Adonais with one word missing, to be supplied from memory

explanation.walkthrough: The line in Adonais is 'Life, like a dome of many-coloured glass, / Stains the white ___ of Eternity'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is a noun for shining brilliance, which Shelley's coloured glass stains.

clue.text: Famous physicist far from old-fashioned?

parts.note: far from old means new
the ton, from French, is the fashion or fashionable society

explanation.surface: A celebrated scientist is anything but behind the times.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Newton, who formulated gravity and the laws of motion, is a celebrated scientist.

clue.text: Unsurpassed sort of 10?

explanation.surface: The best kind of 10.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsurpassed describes a best-ever performance; 10 is a disc, and a gramophone disc is one kind.

clue.text: Not even this bird sang where 11 loitered

definitions.text: Not even this bird sang where 11 loitered

parts.words: Not even this bird sang where 11 loitered
parts.note: Keats writes 'The sedge has withered from the lake, / And no birds sing' where the knight loiters

explanation.surface: Silence by the lake where the knight hung about.
explanation.definitionFit: A small reed-bed songbird is named for the sedge that Keats says has withered.

clue.text: The 11's was a belle

parts.note: the knight's lady is La Belle ..., the beautiful lady

explanation.surface: The knight's beloved was a beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats's title calls her a Belle Dame, French for a lady.

clue.text: Unaccented pull-up ?

parts.note: a roadside stop for lorry drivers is a transport caff, the French word written without its acute accent

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a pull-up is a roadside eating place for drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A snack bar where travellers pull in, written without the French accent mark.

clue.text: The miners with difficulty rouse many

parts.note: the NUM is Britain's National Union of Mineworkers

indicators.note: with difficulty suggests the letters are rearranged laboriously

explanation.surface: The coal-workers' union struggles to stir a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Great in number means many.

clue.text: This wind will oddly enough set in early

indicators.note: the jumbled word is set inside the other one
oddly enough suggests the three letters are arranged strangely

explanation.surface: This breeze will strangely arrive ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly enough' turns SET into STE, which goes inside EARLY after EA.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind blowing from the east is named for its direction.
